title: Low Ly$α$ Visibility in Galaxy Overdensities: Reionization Topology and Neutral-Fraction Ceilings from DIVER over $4.8<z<11$
comment: 30 pages, 17 figures, 3 tables; submitted to ApJ
summary: Ly-alpha emission is widely used to trace cosmic reionization, but its interpretation depends on how Ly-alpha visibility varies with galaxy environment. We use deep JWST/NIRSpec observations from Deep Insights into UV Spectroscopy at the Epoch of Reionization (DIVER) in GOODS-N to measure Ly-alpha visibility for 250 galaxies at 4.8<z<11. The sample contains 84 Ly-alpha detections, including 44 strong emitters with rest-frame Ly-alpha equivalent width W_Lyalpha>25 A. We combine these measurements with H-alpha and [O III] emitters from JWST/NIRCam wide-field slitless spectroscopy to map the density field around each DIVER galaxy. Galaxies with high Ly-alpha equivalent widths (W_Lyalpha>25 A) or high effective Ly-alpha escape fractions (f_esc,Lyalpha^eff>0.05) tend to lie farther from nearby H-alpha and [O III] emitters than galaxies with lower Ly-alpha visibility. The clearest signal occurs near the prominent GOODS-N overdensity at z~5.2, where fewer than 15% of galaxies show strong Ly-alpha emission. This trend is opposite to the simplest inside-out reionization expectation that overdensities produce larger ionized regions and enhance Ly-alpha visibility. Possible explanations include circumgalactic and local intergalactic opacity, dense absorbers, and gas kinematics. We also derive an empirical upper envelope for f_esc,Lyalpha^eff and calibrate it with reionization simulations. Interpreting this envelope as a limiting IGM-attenuation signal gives neutral-fraction ceilings of <x_HI>_max=0.36, 0.76, 0.74, 0.84, and 1.0 at z~5.2, 5.8, 6.7, 7.7, and 9.8, respectively. The z~8 ceiling disfavors an almost completely neutral IGM at this epoch. These results support patchy reionization already underway by z~8 and show that galaxy Ly-alpha visibility encodes both large-scale ionization topology and near-source gas structure.

AI.tldr: Using JWST/NIRSpec observations from the DIVER program in GOODS-N, the authors measure Ly-alpha visibility for 250 galaxies at 4.8<z<11, finding that strong Ly-alpha emitters tend to lie farther from dense environments. Contrary to simple inside-out reionization expectations, overdensities show reduced Ly-alpha visibility, likely due to local IGM opacity and gas kinematics. The empirical upper envelope of Ly-alpha escape fraction yields neutral-fraction ceilings across redshifts, disfavoring a fully neutral IGM at z~8 and supporting patchy reionization underway by that epoch.
AI.motivation: Ly-alpha emission is a crucial tracer of cosmic reionization, but its interpretation depends on how Ly-alpha visibility varies with galaxy environment, which has been poorly constrained at high redshift.
AI.method: Deep JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy (DIVER) in GOODS-N was used to measure Ly-alpha visibility for 250 galaxies at 4.8<z<11, combined with H-alpha and [O III] emitters from JWST/NIRCam slitless spectroscopy to map the density field around each galaxy. An empirical upper envelope for effective Ly-alpha escape fraction was calibrated with reionization simulations.
AI.result: 84 Ly-alpha detections including 44 strong emitters were found. Strong Ly-alpha emitters tend to lie farther from dense environments, most clearly near the z~5.2 GOODS-N overdensity where fewer than 15% of galaxies show strong Ly-alpha emission. Neutral-fraction ceilings of <x_HI>_max=0.36, 0.76, 0.74, 0.84, and 1.0 were derived at z~5.2, 5.8, 6.7, 7.7, and 9.8.
AI.conclusion: The results oppose the simplest inside-out reionization scenario, support patchy reionization already underway by z~8, indicate a not-fully-neutral IGM at z~8, and show that Ly-alpha visibility encodes both large-scale ionization topology and near-source gas structure.

title: A Systematic Gaia--ZTF Search for Short-Period Blue Compact-Binary Candidates
summary: We present a catalog of 147 short-period (10.34--106.46~min) blue compact-binary candidates, identified by combining Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry with ZTF DR23 light curves via a Gaia selection, period searches, and machine-learning morphology ranking. Of these, 111 lack prior compact-binary classifications. Multiwavelength data (DESI DR1, GALEX, AllWISE) reveal a heterogeneous sample: on the Gaia colour--magnitude diagram, 52 sources lie on the white-dwarf locus, 69 in the hot-subdwarf region, and 26 are intermediate. Among 26 sources with DESI spectra, only about one third follow the white-dwarf cooling sequence; the rest are more luminous blue stars with white-dwarf-like low-resolution spectra. We highlight a prioritized subset of new white-dwarf-locus candidates for follow-up, including ten with periods below 40~min and none with existing radial-velocity data. Under fiducial binary assumptions, 17 of these newly identified white-dwarf-locus candidates would exceed the adopted LISA signal-to-noise threshold (led by a 37~pc white dwarf), with the count depending on chirp mass (9 for $0.15\,M_\odot$, 17 for $0.3\,M_\odot$, 21 for $0.6\,M_\odot$), assuming orbital modulation. However, for most of the white-dwarf-locus sample, observed modulation amplitudes exceed any plausible ellipsoidal signal by three to five orders of magnitude, implying that rotating magnetic or chemically inhomogeneous single white dwarfs offer a viable alternative that ZTF photometry alone cannot rule out---the catalog includes at least one confirmed case. We release the full 147-source catalog, including periods, Gaia/spectroscopic classifications, harmonic/ellipsoidal diagnostics, and supplementary tables of fiducial GW estimates and UV--IR photometry.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a catalog of 147 short-period (10–106 min) blue compact-binary candidates compiled from Gaia DR3 astrometry/photometry and ZTF DR23 light curves, using a Gaia selection, period searches, and machine-learning morphology ranking. Of these, 111 are newly classified as compact binaries. Multiwavelength analysis reveals a heterogeneous population (52 white-dwarf locus, 69 hot-subdwarf region, 26 intermediate). Among the white-dwarf-locus candidates, many would exceed the LISA signal-to-noise threshold under binary assumptions, but observed modulation amplitudes are 3–5 orders of magnitude larger than plausible ellipsoidal signals, suggesting rotating magnetic or chemically inhomogeneous single white dwarfs as a viable alternative that ZTF photometry cannot exclude.
AI.motivation: To identify and characterize short-period compact binaries—key gravitational-wave (LISA) sources—by combining Gaia astrometry/photometry with ZTF light curves, and to release a well-vetted catalog for follow-up while assessing whether detected photometric variability genuinely indicates binarity.
AI.method: Combined Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry with ZTF DR23 light curves; performed a Gaia selection, period searches, and machine-learning morphology ranking. Used DESI DR1, GALEX, and AllWISE data for multiwavelength classification, computed harmonic/ellipsoidal diagnostics, and made fiducial gravitational-wave chirp-mass estimates.
AI.result: Produced 147 blue compact-binary candidates (111 without prior classification), classified into white-dwarf locus (52), hot-subdwarf region (69), and intermediate (26). Ten prioritized new white-dwarf-locus candidates have periods below 40 min with no existing radial-velocity data; 17 would exceed the adopted LISA SNR threshold under fiducial binary assumptions. However, modulation amplitudes exceed plausible ellipsoidal signals by 3–5 orders of magnitude for most white-dwarf-locus candidates, indicating rotating magnetic/chemically inhomogeneous single white dwarfs cannot be ruled out; at least one confirmed case exists.
AI.conclusion: The catalog significantly expands the known short-period compact-binary population and highlights promising LISA-relevant white-dwarf-locus candidates, but cautions that ZTF photometry alone cannot distinguish binarity from rotating single magnetic/peculiar white dwarfs in many cases, motivating dedicated spectroscopic/radial-velocity follow-up. The full 147-source catalog and supplementary tables are publicly released.

title: Serendipitous discovery of an almost-dark galaxy in the Virgo Cluster
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A Letters
summary: Analogues of extreme Local Group galaxies with very low surface brightness and large effective radii must exist elsewhere, still hidden due to current detection limits. We report the serendipitous discovery of a low-mass almost-dark galaxy TTT J1237327+143535 in the Virgo Cluster, observed using the Two-meter Twin Telescope at the Teide Observatory. TTT J1237327+143535 has a central surface brightness of $27.9 \pm 0.2 \, \mathrm{mag arcsec}^{-2}$ in the $g'$-band, an effective radius of $0.9 \pm 0.1 \, \mathrm{kpc}$, and a total stellar mass of $(2.2 \pm 0.4) \times 10^6 \, \mathrm{M_\odot}$. Its effective radius and absolute magnitude are similar to those of galaxies And XXI and And XXIII. The discovery of this extremely low surface brightness, extended, low-mass galaxy suggests the existence of a significant population of almost-dark galaxies in the Virgo Cluster. An in-depth analysis of the Next Generation Virgo Cluster survey, as well as upcoming Rubin Data Releases and the 10-year Rubin Legacy Survey of Space and Time are expected to reveal large samples of this extreme galaxy population, which offers insights on galaxy formation in extreme conditions.

AI.tldr: Serendipitous discovery of TTT J1237327+143535, a low-mass almost-dark galaxy in the Virgo Cluster with extremely low surface brightness (27.9 mag arcsec^-2) and large effective radius (0.9 kpc), suggesting a significant hidden population of such galaxies that future surveys (NGVS, Rubin LSST) will uncover.
AI.motivation: Extreme Local Group galaxies with very low surface brightness and large effective radii must exist in other clusters but remain hidden due to current detection limits. Finding such analogues is crucial for understanding galaxy formation in extreme low-luminosity regimes.
AI.method: Serendipitous detection using the Two-meter Twin Telescope at the Teide Observatory, followed by measurement of photometric and structural properties (central surface brightness, effective radius, total stellar mass) in the g'-band, and comparison with Local Group galaxies.
AI.result: TTT J1237327+143535 has a central surface brightness of 27.9±0.2 mag arcsec^-2, effective radius of 0.9±0.1 kpc, and stellar mass of (2.2±0.4)×10^6 M_sun, making it similar in size and magnitude to And XXI and And XXIII.
AI.conclusion: The discovery implies a significant population of almost-dark galaxies exists in the Virgo Cluster. Deeper surveys, including NGVS analysis and Rubin LSST data releases, are expected to reveal large samples of this extreme population, offering new insights into galaxy formation under extreme conditions.

title: Non-ideal MHD and protostellar feedback effects on disc formation and evolution in numerical simulations of star cluster formation
comment: 35 pages, 39 figures. Accepted for publication in MNRAS. Published version available at https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stag1501
summary: While recent surveys have resolved hundreds of nearby protostellar discs, numerical simulations assuming ideal magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) have historically struggled to achieve disc formation due to efficient angular momentum removal by magnetic torques. Non-ideal MHD effects, relevant at the low ionization fractions typical of molecular clouds, have been shown to reduce the effectiveness of magnetic braking and promote disc formation. In this work, we present the results from a suite of calculations following the gravitational collapse of 50 $M_{\odot}$ turbulent molecular cloud cores down to the formation and evolution of stellar systems and protostellar discs. We use the radiation-MHD code GIZMO including non-ideal MHD (Ohmic resistivity, ambipolar diffusion, and the Hall effect) and the STARFORGE numerical framework for modeling star formation and stellar feedback. We compare the effects of assuming ideal vs. non-ideal MHD and including sub-grid protostellar jet feedback on disc formation and evolution. Discs form in all of our models but are least massive in the model with ideal MHD and sub-grid jet feedback. Apart from the ideal MHD$+$jets model, we do not observe any significant differences in disc properties between the ideal and non-ideal MHD models; however, ideal MHD discs are embedded in smaller rotating envelopes. Disc sizes are in general agreement with those of observed discs. Jet feedback increases core fragmentation and reduces final stellar masses. Our results suggest that magnetic braking does not efficiently suppress disc formation, regardless of whether ideal or non-ideal MHD is assumed, under the dynamical conditions in which multiple stellar systems form.

AI.tldr: This study uses radiation-MHD simulations with GIZMO and the STARFORGE framework to model the collapse of 50 M☉ turbulent cores into stellar systems and protostellar discs, comparing ideal vs. non-ideal MHD and the presence/absence of sub-grid protostellar jet feedback. Discs form in all models, with the least massive discs occurring in the ideal MHD + jets case. Aside from that model, disc properties are largely similar across ideal and non-ideal MHD setups, though ideal MHD discs inhabit smaller rotating envelopes. Jet feedback enhances core fragmentation and lowers final stellar masses. Overall, magnetic braking does not efficiently suppress disc formation under the dynamical conditions of multiple stellar system formation.
AI.motivation: Previous numerical simulations assuming ideal MHD struggled to form protostellar discs due to efficient magnetic braking removing angular momentum. This work aims to investigate whether non-ideal MHD effects and jet feedback can alleviate this problem and promote disc formation under realistic turbulent core collapse conditions.
AI.method: A suite of calculations is performed following the gravitational collapse of 50 M☉ turbulent molecular cloud cores using the radiation-MHD code GIZMO, including non-ideal MHD (Ohmic resistivity, ambipolar diffusion, and the Hall effect) and the STARFORGE framework for star formation and stellar feedback. Four models combine ideal vs. non-ideal MHD with or without sub-grid protostellar jet feedback, and their disc formation and evolution properties are compared.
AI.result: Discs form in all models, with the smallest masses in the ideal MHD + jets case. No significant differences in disc properties are seen between ideal and non-ideal MHD models except that ideal MHD discs are embedded in smaller rotating envelopes. Disc sizes generally match observed discs. Jet feedback increases core fragmentation and reduces final stellar masses.
AI.conclusion: Magnetic braking does not efficiently suppress disc formation regardless of whether ideal or non-ideal MHD is assumed, under the dynamical conditions in which multiple stellar systems form. This challenges the historical notion that ideal MHD alone inhibits disc formation and suggests other dynamical factors dominate.

title: Reconstructing orbits of galaxies in extreme regions (roger v2.0): an extension to intermediate mass systems
comment: Code hosted at https://github.com/Martindelosrios/pyROGER. Prepared for submission to MNRAS
summary: In this paper, we present an updated version of the roger code, called roger v2.0, developed to perform the orbital classification of galaxies residing in and around galaxy groups and clusters. In addition to the projected phase-space coordinates, the new version incorporates the host halo mass as an additional input parameter. Although the inclusion of the halo mass leads to only modest changes in the classification, it contributes to improving the overall robustness of the method. We also extend the range of host halo masses over which roger can be applied, enabling the analysis of systems with masses down to $10^{13.5} h^{-1} M_{\odot}$. We further provide a Python implementation of the new code, which will be made publicly available. This implementation enables users to efficiently and robustly classify arbitrary galaxy samples using either version of the method. Moreover, it allows users to train a customized classifier on an alternative training set, providing the flexibility to adapt the method to different datasets and scientific applications.

AI.tldr: This paper presents roger v2.0, an updated code for orbital classification of galaxies in and around groups and clusters. It adds host halo mass as an additional input parameter alongside projected phase-space coordinates, extends applicability to lower-mass systems ($10^{13.5} h^{-1} M_{\odot}$), and provides a publicly available Python implementation with customizable training capabilities.
AI.motivation: To improve the robustness and versatility of the existing roger code for classifying galaxy orbits in group/cluster environments by incorporating additional physical information (halo mass) and extending its range of applicability to lower-mass halos, while making the tool more accessible through a Python implementation.
AI.method: The updated roger v2.0 code incorporates host halo mass as an additional input parameter alongside the projected phase-space coordinates used in the original version. A Python implementation is provided that supports both versions of the method, allows classification of arbitrary galaxy samples, and permits users to train customized classifiers on alternative training sets.
AI.result: The inclusion of halo mass leads to modest changes in classification but improves overall method robustness. The code can now analyze systems with host halo masses down to $10^{13.5} h^{-1} M_{\odot}$, extending its range of application. A publicly available Python implementation enables efficient and robust classification of arbitrary galaxy samples.
AI.conclusion: roger v2.0 offers an improved, more robust orbital classification tool with extended mass-range applicability, delivered as a flexible Python package that can be used out-of-the-box or retrained on custom datasets for diverse scientific applications.

title: The Kick Velocities of Neutron Stars in Binary Systems
comment: 38 pages, 23 figures, to be submitted to ApJ
summary: Neutron stars (NSs) receive natal kicks on their formation in supernovae (SNe). We consider constraints placed on the natal kick magnitudes by NSs in different kinds of binary systems. We compare observed systems to predictions from the COMPAS rapid population synthesis code, where we apply kick models with varied natal kick prescriptions. Specifically, we compare binary orbits (i.e., periods and eccentricities) and systemic kick estimates of (1) Gaia observations of NS-harboring binaries (Gaia NSs), (2) NS low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs), (3) NS-white dwarf binaries (NSWDs), (4) NS high-mass X-ray binaries (HMXBs) and in particular Be X-ray binaries (BeXBs), and (5) double NSs (DNSs). In this comparison, we find that we can reproduce most of the observed properties of the Gaia NSs, LMXBs, and NSWDs with natal kicks calibrated to the velocities of young isolated pulsars, although we need "rocket" kicks to explain the Gaia NS eccentricities. The HMXBs and DNSs, in contrast, show evidence of significantly reduced NS natal kicks. In particular, we find that an apparent correlation between eccentricity and systemic kick for DNSs can be explained by Blaauw kicks, if the natal kicks are ${\lesssim}\,10\,$km$\,$s$^{-1}$. Although our model does not align well with low-metallicity Gaia NSs, high-eccentricity BeXBs, and DNS mass estimates, we provide alternative hypothetical explanations for these systems. We conclude that a model in which NSs that are formed in binaries with high-mass companions receive significantly reduced natal kicks can provide a relatively consistent explanation for the observed NSs in binary systems.

AI.tldr: This paper uses the COMPAS rapid population synthesis code to constrain neutron star natal kick magnitudes by comparing predicted binary properties (periods, eccentricities, systemic kicks) against observations of various NS-harboring binary systems, including Gaia NSs, LMXBs, NSWDs, HMXBs/BeXBs, and DNSs. The authors find that while a universal kick model calibrated to young isolated pulsars works for Gaia NSs (with "rocket" kicks needed for eccentricities), LMXBs, and NSWDs, HMXBs and DNSs require significantly reduced natal kicks (≲10 km/s for DNSs), leading to the conclusion that NSs formed in binaries with massive companions receive substantially diminished natal kicks.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to determine what constraints different types of NS-harboring binary systems place on natal kick magnitudes, and to test whether a single universal kick prescription can explain all observed NS binary populations or whether kick magnitudes vary by formation channel.
AI.method: The study uses the COMPAS rapid population synthesis code with varied natal kick prescriptions to generate predictions for binary orbits and systemic kicks, comparing these against observations of five classes of NS binaries: Gaia NSs, NS LMXBs, NSWDs, HMXBs/BeXBs, and DNSs. Statistical comparisons of period, eccentricity, and systemic velocity distributions are used to constrain kick models.
AI.result: A kick model calibrated to young isolated pulsar velocities reproduces most properties of Gaia NSs, LMXBs, and NSWDs, though exotic "rocket" kicks are needed to explain Gaia NS eccentricities. Conversely, HMXBs and DNSs require significantly reduced natal kicks. The DNS eccentricity–systemic kick correlation is explained by Blaauw kicks if natal kicks are ≲10 km/s. Some discrepancies remain for low-metallicity Gaia NSs, high-eccentricity BeXBs, and DNS mass estimates.
AI.conclusion: The authors conclude that a kick prescription in which NSs formed in binaries with high-mass companions experience significantly reduced natal kicks provides a relatively consistent explanation across all observed NS binary populations, suggesting that kick magnitude depends on the companion mass or binary environment at the time of supernova.

title: Tracing Lyman alpha escape in the CRISTAL-02 galaxy at z~5.3
comment: 13 pages, 8 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary:
Aim. We investigate the mechanisms regulating Lyman-alpha (Ly-a) escape in the star-forming galaxy CRISTAL-02 at z~5.3. The galaxy hosts five distinct clumps, with Clumps A and B suggested as potential active galactic nuclei (AGN) candidates. We study how AGN or star formation activity influences the spatial distribution and escape of Ly-a emission.
  Methods. Using VLT/MUSE Ly-a and JWST/NIRSpec IFU H-a and H-b observations, complemented by NIRCam UV imaging, we constructed spatially matched emission-line maps. We derived flux, line-ratio, and extinction maps, together with spatially resolved Ly-a escape fractions and ionizing photon production efficiencies.
  Results. Ly-a emission extends preferentially along the [C ii] outflow direction, while H-a and UV trace the galactic disk. Clumps A and B show contrasting properties: Clump A, with lower dust attenuation, exhibits enhanced Ly-a/H-a ratios and a higher Ly-a escape fraction, whereas Clump B shows stronger H-a and UV emission but suppressed Ly-a. These results suggest that Ly-a escape is influenced by outflows, dust attenuation, and local gas conditions.
  Conclusions. We present spatially resolved measurements of the Ly-a escape fraction and ionizing photon production efficiency in a galaxy at z~5.3, highlighting the role of feedback-driven gas clearing and anisotropic outflows in shaping Ly-a emission. The evidence favors an outflow, but the available data cannot uniquely distinguish between AGN- and star formation-driven feedback. Future spatially resolved Ly-a, H-a, and [C ii] observations will be crucial for identifying the dominant feedback mechanism.

AI.tldr: This study investigates Ly-alpha escape mechanisms in the z~5.3 star-forming galaxy CRISTAL-02 using VLT/MUSE, JWST/NIRSpec IFU, and NIRCam data. Key results include: Ly-alpha emission extends preferentially along the [C ii] outflow direction while Ha and UV trace the disk; Clump A (low dust) shows enhanced Ly-alpha escape while Clump B shows suppressed Ly-alpha despite stronger continuum emission; spatially resolved Ly-alpha escape fractions and ionizing photon production efficiencies are presented. The evidence favors outflow-driven gas clearing and anisotropic geometry, but AGN versus star-formation-driven feedback cannot be uniquely distinguished.
AI.motivation: To understand what regulates Lyman-alpha escape in high-redshift star-forming galaxies, specifically whether AGN or star formation activity drives the spatial distribution and escape of Ly-alpha emission in CRISTAL-02 at z~5.3.
AI.method: Spatially matched emission-line maps were constructed from VLT/MUSE Ly-alpha and JWST/NIRSpec IFU Ha and Hb observations, complemented by NIRCam UV imaging. Flux, line-ratio, extinction, spatially resolved Ly-alpha escape fraction, and ionizing photon production efficiency maps were derived.
AI.result: Ly-alpha preferentially escapes along the [C ii] outflow direction, whereas Ha and UV trace the galactic disk. Clump A (low dust attenuation) shows enhanced Ly-alpha/Ha ratios and higher escape fractions, while Clump B shows stronger Ha/UV but suppressed Ly-alpha. The role of outflows, dust attenuation, and local gas conditions in shaping Ly-alpha escape is demonstrated.
AI.conclusion: Feedback-driven gas clearing and anisotropic outflows shape Ly-alpha emission in CRISTAL-02. The evidence favors an outflow interpretation, but AGN and star-formation-driven feedback cannot be distinguished with the current data. Future spatially resolved Ly-alpha, Ha, and [C ii] observations are needed to identify the dominant feedback mechanism.

title: SN 2021pfs: A Type Ia Supernova Likely Affected by Progenitor Metallicity, as Revealed by Comparison with Its Twin Counterpart
comment: 35 pages, 14 figures, published in SCIENCE CHINA Physics, Mechanics & Astronomy,DOI: 10.1007/s11433-026-2999-3
summary: We present extensive photometric and spectroscopic observations of the normal type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) 2021pfs, which occurred in the Seyfert 2 galaxy NGC 5427 at a redshift 0.009. SN 2021pfs reached an absolute \textit{B}-band peak magnitude of $M_{\rm max}(B)=$-19.28 $\pm$ 0.40 mag. The mag and a post-peak decline rate of $Δm_{15}(B)=$1.13 $\pm$ 0.06 mag. The observed properties of this nearby SN Ia closely resemble those of SN 2011fe, including the main optical spectroscopic features and photometric evolution. Despite their similar decline rates, SN 2021pfs rose more rapidly in the $U$ band but more slowly in the $r$ and $i$ bands compared to SN 2011fe in very early phases. This photometric difference, particularly at short wavelengths, can introduce a systematic uncertainty of up to $\sim$12% in distance estimates. Analysis of the host galaxy's local and global environment shows an environment consistent with producing a higher-metallicity progenitor for SN 2021pfs than that of SN 2011fe.This higher progenitor metallicity may explain the observed photometric discrepancy and the resulting distance between SN 2021pfs and SN 2011fe, though a larger sample of such "twin" SNe Ia is needed to confirm this trend and assess its impact on cosmological measurements.

AI.tldr: This paper presents detailed photometric and spectroscopic observations of SN 2021pfs, a normal Type Ia supernova in the Seyfert 2 galaxy NGC 5427 at redshift 0.009. It closely resembles SN 2011fe in optical spectra and photometric evolution, but shows differences in early-phase U/r/i-band rise rates. The host environment suggests a higher-metallicity progenitor, which may explain these photometric discrepancies and cause up to ~12% systematic uncertainty in distance estimates.
AI.motivation: The study aims to characterize a normal Type Ia supernova (SN 2021pfs) that serves as a "twin" to the well-known SN 2011fe, to understand how progenitor metallicity and local environment affect photometric properties and introduce systematic uncertainties in distance measurements, which are critical for cosmological applications.
AI.method: The authors conducted extensive photometric and spectroscopic observations of SN 2021pfs, measured its light-curve parameters (peak magnitude, decline rate Δm15(B)), compared its photometric evolution and spectral features against SN 2011fe, and analyzed both local and global host galaxy environments to infer progenitor metallicity.
AI.result: SN 2021pfs peaked at Mmax(B) = -19.28 ± 0.40 mag with Δm15(B) = 1.13 ± 0.06 mag. Despite overall similarity to SN 2011fe, it rose faster in the U band but slower in the r and i bands at early phases. The photometric differences could introduce up to ~12% systematic uncertainty in distance estimates. The host environment is consistent with a higher-metallicity progenitor than SN 2011fe.
AI.conclusion: The higher progenitor metallicity of SN 2021pfs compared to SN 2011fe likely explains the observed photometric discrepancies and distance-estimation errors. A larger sample of such twin SNe Ia is needed to confirm this trend and assess its impact on cosmological distance measurements.

title: The VariableTNG project: mass-dependent regulation of galaxy morphology by baryonic feedback
summary: Galaxy morphology is shaped by both assembly history and baryonic processes, but their relative roles remain uncertain. We use the VariableTNG (VTNG) simulation suite to investigate how variations in baryonic feedback regulate galaxy morphology while keeping the initial conditions fixed. VTNG consists of cosmological magnetohydrodynamic simulations performed with the moving-mesh code {\sc AREPO}, varying eight parameters governing stellar and AGN feedback. At $z=1$, we characterize morphology using $κ_{\rm co}$, $v/σ$, and the axis ratio $c/a$. We find substantial morphological diversity across feedback models, with the dominant mechanism strongly dependent on stellar mass. For $M_\ast \lesssim 10^{11}\,{\rm M_\odot}$, morphology is primarily controlled by the supernova temperature $T_{\rm SN}$: larger $T_{\rm SN}$ delays early star formation, promotes a denser and more rotationally supported gas reservoir, and favours subsequent disc growth through in-situ star formation. At higher masses, morphology becomes increasingly sensitive to AGN feedback, particularly the quasar-mode coupling efficiency $ε_{\rm f,high}$. Higher $ε_{\rm f,high}$ suppresses early black hole growth, thereby weakening subsequent radio-mode feedback associated with gas depletion and loss of rotational support. The resulting morphology--mass relation is non-monotonic, with maximum rotational support at intermediate stellar masses. Our results demonstrate that baryonic feedback regulates galaxy morphology through distinct mass-dependent pathways, with stellar feedback dominating at lower masses and AGN self-regulation becoming increasingly important at the massive end.

AI.tldr: Using the VariableTNG (VTNG) simulation suite with fixed initial conditions but varied baryonic feedback parameters, this paper shows that galaxy morphology at z=1 is regulated through mass-dependent pathways: supernova temperature (T_SN) dominates morphology control below ~10^11 M_sun, while quasar-mode AGN feedback coupling efficiency (ε_f,high) dominates at higher masses, producing a non-monotonic morphology-mass relation with maximal rotational support at intermediate masses.
AI.motivation: To disentangle the relative roles of assembly history versus baryonic processes in shaping galaxy morphology, given that this relationship remains poorly understood despite its fundamental importance for galaxy evolution.
AI.method: The authors use the VariableTNG (VTNG) suite of cosmological magnetohydrodynamic simulations run with the AREPO moving-mesh code, varying eight stellar and AGN feedback parameters while keeping initial conditions fixed. Morphology at z=1 is quantified using κ_co, v/σ, and the axis ratio c/a.
AI.result: Substantial morphological diversity arises across feedback models. Below 10^11 M_sun, morphology is primarily governed by supernova temperature, where higher T_SN delays early star formation, creating denser, more rotationally supported gas that favors disc growth. At higher masses, quasar-mode coupling efficiency (ε_f,high) dominates: higher values suppress early black hole growth and weaken subsequent radio-mode feedback, preserving rotational support. The morphology-mass relation is non-monotonic with peak rotational support at intermediate masses.
AI.conclusion: Baryonic feedback regulates galaxy morphology through distinct, mass-dependent mechanisms—stellar feedback dominates at lower masses while AGN self-regulation becomes increasingly important at the massive end—underscoring that feedback physics is a critical driver of morphological diversity independent of assembly history.

title: Chromospheric heating and magnetic topology above the shared penumbra of a delta-spot: Multi-line inversions and multi-height magnetic-field extrapolations
summary: We analysed observations of the Fe I 617.3 nm, Ca II 854.2 nm, and Ca II H lines obtained with CRISP and CHROMIS at the SST. Spatially coupled non-LTE inversions constrained the chromospheric atmosphere, while the WFA provided estimates of the chromospheric line-of-sight magnetic field. We combined these photospheric and chromospheric constraints with an HMI magnetogram as input to a multi-height field extrapolation. We characterised the reconstructed topology using the twist number, squashing factor, current density, and field-line connectivity. Results. The Ca II H magnetic signal is concentrated mainly above the strongest photospheric field concentrations, whereas Ca II 854.2 nm yields stronger and more spatially extended line-of-sight fields. The chromosphere above the shared penumbra is approximately 300 K hotter than nearby quiet regions. The selected brightening follows a chromospheric loop, with enhanced temperature and a transition from blueshift to redshift along the structure. The extrapolation recovers field strengths broadly consistent with the inversions and reveals a left-handed, flux-rope-like core following the polarity inversion line. Enhanced currents and connectivity gradients occur near parts of its boundary, where field lines connect the twisted structure to overarching loops. Conclusions. The temperature and velocity patterns and magnetic topology are consistent with reconnection between the twisted polarity-inversion-line field and the surrounding loops, depositing energy in the chromosphere and driving plasma along reconfigured field lines. These signatures do not uniquely establish reconnection, but show that combining high-resolution spectropolarimetric inversions with multi-height extrapolations can relate chromospheric energy release to the local three-dimensional magnetic structure.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes high-resolution spectropolarimetric observations of Fe I 617.3 nm, Ca II 854.2 nm, and Ca II H lines using non-LTE inversions and magnetic field extrapolations to characterize the chromospheric magnetic topology above a sunspot/shared penumbra region, revealing a left-handed flux-rope-like core, enhanced currents, and signatures consistent with reconnection between twisted magnetic fields and surrounding loops.
AI.motivation: To understand how magnetic energy is released in the chromosphere and relate local energy deposition and plasma flows to the three-dimensional magnetic field structure using combined photospheric and chromospheric observations with multi-height extrapolations.
AI.method: Spatially coupled non-LTE inversions of CRISP/CHROMIS SST data (Fe I 617.3 nm, Ca II 854.2 nm, Ca II H) constrained the chromosphere; the weak-field approximation (WFA) estimated chromospheric line-of-sight magnetic fields; photospheric and chromospheric constraints were combined with an HMI magnetogram for multi-height field extrapolation. Topology was characterized using twist number, squashing factor, current density, and field-line connectivity.
AI.result: Ca II H magnetic signal concentrates above the strongest photospheric fields while Ca II 854.2 nm shows stronger and more extended line-of-sight fields. The chromosphere above the shared penumbra is ~300 K hotter than quiet regions. The brightening follows a chromospheric loop with enhanced temperature and a blueshift-to-redshift transition. Extrapolation recovers field strengths consistent with inversions and reveals a left-handed flux-rope-like core along the polarity inversion line, with enhanced currents and connectivity gradients near its boundary where field lines connect to overarching loops.
AI.conclusion: Temperature, velocity, and magnetic topology patterns are consistent with reconnection between the twisted polarity-inversion-line field and surrounding loops, depositing energy in the chromosphere and driving plasma along reconfigured field lines. While not uniquely establishing reconnection, the study demonstrates that combining high-resolution spectropolarimetric inversions with multi-height extrapolations can link chromospheric energy release to the local 3D magnetic structure.

title: The UKIRT M33 Monitoring Project: A 15-Year Near-Infrared Variable Star Catalogue for the Central Kiloparsec, and Prospects for Star Formation History and Dust Return
comment: To appear in the Proceedings of IAU Symposium 405, Traversing the Galactic Center in Space and Time
summary: We present results from the UKIRT M33 Monitoring Project, a near-infrared survey of variable red giants in the Local Group spiral galaxy M33. Combining four independent photometric datasets spanning UIST (2003), UFTI (2005), WFCAM (2005-2007), and a new UKIRT Hemisphere Survey epoch (2018), we construct a homogenised 15.11-year $K$-band light-curve catalogue for 847 stars in the central kiloparsec, of which 771 (91 per cent) are variable. Cross-matching with archival Spitzer photometry identifies 120 dust-enshrouded AGB candidates. We compare the spatial coverage of this central catalogue with the earlier UIST-only (Paper I) and disc-wide WFCAM (Paper IV) variable-star surveys. Building on this catalogue, two forthcoming papers will (i) measure individual pulsation periods to reconstruct the star formation history of the central kiloparsec, and (ii) refine dust and gas mass-loss rates across the disc using the extended time baseline.

AI.tldr: The UKIRT M33 Monitoring Project combines four photometric datasets spanning 15.11 years to construct a homogeneous K-band light-curve catalogue of 847 red giants in the central kiloparsec of M33, of which 91% are variable, and identifies 120 dust-enshrouded AGB candidates via cross-matching with Spitzer. Two forthcoming papers will use this catalogue to measure pulsation periods for star formation history reconstruction and to refine mass-loss rates.
AI.motivation: To create a long-baseline, homogenised near-infrared light-curve catalogue of variable red giants in the central region of M33, enabling studies of star formation history and stellar mass loss in a Local Group spiral galaxy.
AI.method: Combining four independent photometric datasets (UIST 2003, UFTI 2005, WFCAM 2005-2007, and UKIRT Hemisphere Survey 2018) into a homogenised 15.11-year K-band light-curve catalogue, cross-matched with archival Spitzer photometry to identify dust-enshrouded AGB candidates, and compared with earlier surveys for spatial coverage.
AI.result: A catalogue of 847 stars was constructed, with 771 (91%) found to be variable. Cross-matching identified 120 dust-enshrouded AGB candidates. The catalogue's spatial coverage was compared with earlier UIST-only (Paper I) and disc-wide WFCAM (Paper IV) variable-star surveys.
AI.conclusion: The extended time baseline and homogeneous catalogue set the stage for two forthcoming papers that will measure pulsation periods to reconstruct the star formation history of the central kiloparsec and refine dust/gas mass-loss rates across the M33 disc.

title: Toward Operational Solar Flare Peak Flux Nowcasting: A Strategy Combining Real-Time Data, Machine Learning, and NOAA Flare Detection Criteria
summary: We present the RMN strategy (Real-time data, machine learning, and NOAA flare detection criteria) for nowcasting the peak soft X-ray flux of ongoing solar flares under operationally realistic conditions. The strategy combines real-time GOES 0.1-0.8 nm X-ray observations with an attention-based sequence-to-sequence Long Short-Term Memory model. Under the NOAA flare detection criteria, predictions are evaluated at one-minute intervals from three minutes after the cataloged onset to the observed peak using the preceding 60 minutes of X-ray observations. We apply the RMN strategy to C-, M-, and X-class flares observed by GOES-8-18 from 1997 to 2024 using four-fold cross-validation. The major results of this study are as follows. First, the model nowcasts peak soft X-ray flux with RMSE and PE values of 0.26 and 3.11\% for the $\geq$C-class group, 0.45 and 5.59\% for the $\geq$M-class group, and 0.87 and 12.76\% for the X-class group. The higher discrepancy toward stronger flare groups indicates that peak-flux prediction is more challenging for higher-intensity flares. Second, the model performance depends on flare rise time and prediction time, with larger errors for longer rise time events and improved performance as the prediction time approaches the flare peak. Shorter rise time events approach their final peak more rapidly, providing a clearer indication of the eventual peak, whereas the larger difference for longer rise time events may partly reflect more complex temporal evolution. Third, empirical coverage based on total uncertainty remains high but decreases for stronger flares, with noise uncertainty contributing more than model uncertainty.

AI.tldr: The paper presents the RMN strategy (Real-time data, machine learning, NOAA flare detection criteria) for nowcasting peak soft X-ray flux of ongoing solar flares. Using an attention-based sequence-to-sequence LSTM model with real-time GOES X-ray observations, the method achieves RMSE of 0.26, 0.45, and 0.87 for C-, M-, and X-class flares respectively, with performance degrading for stronger flares and longer rise times.
AI.motivation: To provide real-time nowcasting of peak soft X-ray flux for ongoing solar flares under operationally realistic conditions, addressing the challenge that peak-flux prediction becomes more difficult for higher-intensity flares and that performance depends on flare rise time and prediction time.
AI.method: Combines real-time GOES 0.1-0.8 nm X-ray observations with an attention-based sequence-to-sequence Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model. Predictions are evaluated at one-minute intervals from three minutes after cataloged onset to the observed peak, using the preceding 60 minutes of X-ray observations under NOAA flare detection criteria. Validated using four-fold cross-validation on C-, M-, and X-class flares from GOES-8-18 (1997-2024).
AI.result: RMSE and PE values are 0.26 and 3.11% for the C-class group, 0.45 and 5.59% for the M-class group, and 0.87 and 12.76% for the X-class group. Larger errors are found for longer rise time events, with improved performance as prediction time approaches the flare peak. Empirical coverage based on total uncertainty remains high but decreases for stronger flares, with noise uncertainty dominating over model uncertainty.
AI.conclusion: The RMN strategy effectively nowcasts peak soft X-ray flux for ongoing solar flares, but accuracy decreases for higher-intensity flares and longer rise time events. Predictive performance improves as the prediction time approaches the flare peak, and noise uncertainty is the dominant source of total uncertainty.

title: Diversity of Ionized Gas Structures in Nearby Metal-poor Dwarf Galaxies
comment: 15 pages, 5 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to PASJ. Comments are very welcome!
summary: We investigate whether optical and far-infrared [O III] emission from nearby metal-poor dwarf galaxies can be represented by a homogeneous one-zone ionized-gas model with a single electron temperature and density. Our sample comprises five galaxies from the Herschel Dwarf Galaxy Survey: HS1222+3741, SBS0335-052E, POX186, Haro11, and IZw18. We combine galaxy-integrated or nearly galaxy-integrated [O III] 4363 and 5007 measurements from Seimei/KOOLS-IFU observations and published or archival spectroscopy with Herschel/PACS [O III] 88um measurements. Because [O III] 4363 is not detected in HS1222+3741, the analysis is based on the remaining four galaxies. SBS0335-052E and Haro11 lie near or slightly beyond the low-density boundary of the one-zone diagnostic. Their nominal line ratios favor effective densities of ne<1cm-3, while conservative treatment of the uncertainties allows values up to 40 and 10cm-3, respectively. These remain substantially below densities inferred from independent diagnostics. By contrast, POX186 and IZw18 show no significant discrepancy between the optical--far-infrared [O III] and low-ionization optical diagnostics. Additional optical and ultraviolet diagnostics show that inferred densities can span several orders of magnitude within a galaxy. Representative two-zone models reproduce the [O III] 4363, 5007, and 88um emission in SBS0335-052E and Haro11 by combining relatively dense gas with cooler, low-density gas. The low-density component contributes approximately 61% and 72% of the 88um luminosity, but only 14% and 23% of the 5007 luminosity, respectively. These solutions are not unique and may represent a broader unresolved distribution of gas conditions. Our results show that temperatures and densities inferred from integrated one-zone analyses are effective quantities and that similar diagnostic discrepancies can arise in nearby metal-poor galaxies.

AI.tldr: This paper tests whether optical and far-infrared [O III] emission from nearby metal-poor dwarf galaxies can be explained by a homogeneous one-zone ionized-gas model with a single electron temperature and density. Using [O III] 4363/5007 from Seimei/KOOLS-IFU and [O III] 88um from Herschel/PACS for four galaxies, they find that SBS0335-052E and Haro11 show discrepancies between diagnostics (favoring very low densities), while POX186 and IZw18 are consistent. Two-zone models reproduce the observations, showing that one-zone-derived densities/temperatures are only effective quantities.
AI.motivation: To determine whether integrated one-zone models with a single electron temperature and density can adequately represent the ionized gas in nearby metal-poor dwarf galaxies, given that such models are commonly used but may not capture the true complexity of the gas conditions.
AI.method: The authors combine galaxy-integrated [O III] 4363 and 5007 measurements from Seimei/KOOLS-IFU with published/archival spectroscopy and Herschel/PACS [O III] 88um data for five galaxies (four usable: SBS0335-052E, POX186, Haro11, IZw18). They compare one-zone diagnostics against low-ionization optical diagnostics and construct representative two-zone models.
AI.result: SBS0335-052E and Haro11 fall near or beyond the low-density boundary of the one-zone diagnostic, favoring ne<1 cm-3 nominally (up to 40 and 10 cm-3 with uncertainties), well below densities from independent diagnostics. POX186 and IZw18 show no such discrepancy. Two-zone models with dense + cool low-density gas reproduce observed line ratios; the low-density component contributes 61%/72% of 88um luminosity but only 14%/23% of 5007 luminosity for SBS0335-052E/Haro11. Solutions are non-unique.
AI.conclusion: Temperatures and densities from integrated one-zone analyses are effective quantities, not true physical values. Similar diagnostic discrepancies can arise in nearby metal-poor galaxies, warranting multi-zone or resolved treatments of the ionized gas.

title: ALOHA IRDCs Molecular Line Follow-up: I. Gas properties and kinematics
comment: 11 pages, 3 figures, accepted for publication on A&A
summary: Infrared Dark Clouds are ideal sites for investigating the initial conditions of massive star and cluster formation. The A Lei Of the Habitat and Assembly of Infrared Dark Clouds (ALOHA IRDCs), a James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT) Large Program, has mapped nearby IRDCs with SCUBA-2. Complementary molecular line observations are needed to characterise the physical, kinematic, and chemical properties of the dense gas. We aim to determine the thermal, kinematic, and chemical properties of clumps identified in the ALOHA IRDCs, and to assess their evolutionary status and level of star-forming activity. We performed single-pointing K-band and W-band observations towards 56 ALOHA IRDCs clumps using the Effelsberg 100-m and Yebes 40-m telescopes, respectively. We derived NH3 kinetic temperatures using the hyperfine group ratio (HFGR) method and identified infall and shock signatures from HCO+, H13CO+, SiO, and HNCO profiles. Water masers and NH2D emission were used as complementary tracers of chemical evolution and star formation. The clumps exhibit kinetic temperatures of 15-29 K. We detect NH2D emission towards 18 sources, with NH2D centroid velocities consistent with NH3, indicating both species trace the same dense gas component. More than half of the clumps display blue-asymmetric HCO+ profiles, identifying them as infall candidates. Water masers are detected in 22 sources, with prominent velocity ranges and variability. Broad SiO emission (>~20 km/s) indicates strong shocks, while narrower extents (<~6km/s) likely trace large-scale interactions or low-velocity shocks. The widespread infall signatures, shock tracers, masers, and NH2D emission suggest that relatively quiescent, chemically young material can coexist with dynamically active gas affected by early protostellar feedback, providing insight into the coupled physical and chemical evolution of massive IRDC clumps.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the physical, kinematic, and chemical properties of 56 clumps in Infrared Dark Clouds (IRDCs) observed as part of the ALOHA IRDC Large Program, using single-pointing NH3, HCO+, H13CO+, SiO, and HNCO observations from the Effelsberg 100-m and Yebes 40-m telescopes. Clumps show kinetic temperatures of 15–29 K, with widespread infall signatures, shock tracers, water masers, and NH2D emission, indicating coexistence of chemically young quiescent material with dynamically active gas influenced by early protostellar feedback.
AI.motivation: IRDCs are prime sites to study the initial conditions of massive star and cluster formation. The ALOHA IRDC program mapped these clouds with SCUBA-2, but complementary molecular line observations are needed to characterize the physical, kinematic, and chemical properties of the dense gas and to assess evolutionary status and star-forming activity of the identified clumps.
AI.method: Single-pointing K-band (Effelsberg 100-m) and W-band (Yebes 40-m) observations were performed towards 56 ALOHA IRDC clumps. NH3 kinetic temperatures were derived using the hyperfine group ratio (HFGR) method. Infall and shock signatures were identified from HCO+, H13CO+, SiO, and HNCO profiles. Water masers and NH2D emission served as complementary tracers of chemical evolution and star formation.
AI.result: Clumps exhibit kinetic temperatures of 15–29 K. NH2D was detected towards 18 sources with centroid velocities consistent with NH3. More than half of the clumps show blue-asymmetric HCO+ profiles indicating infall candidates. Water masers were detected in 22 sources. Broad SiO emission (>20 km/s) indicates strong shocks, while narrower extents (<6 km/s) trace large-scale interactions or low-velocity shocks.
AI.conclusion: The coexistence of widespread infall signatures, shock tracers, masers, and NH2D emission suggests that relatively quiescent, chemically young material can exist alongside dynamically active gas affected by early protostellar feedback, providing insight into the coupled physical and chemical evolution of massive IRDC clumps.

title: OutThere Survey: Addressing $\mathrm{ξ_{ion}}$ and $\mathrm{f_{esc}}$ with a population of average galaxies at z$\sim$2
summary: Constraining the major contributors to the ionisation of the early universe is an ongoing endeavour of high-redshift galaxy research. We measure the ionising photon production efficiency and Lyman Continuum escape fraction for a sample of 230 intermediate redshift ($1.3<z<2.6$) sources observed as a part of the \textit{OutThere survey}; a pure-parallel, wide-area JWST/NIRISS survey with accompanying JWST/NIRCam, NIRISS and HST photometry. The low threshold emission selection criteria for this sample makes for a large and robust control, against which other works may be contrasted, particularly for low-mass galaxies above z$>$5. This control sample allows us to verify the correlations between ionising and spectral/physical properties suggested by previous studies. We find no significant correlations between the ionising photon production efficiency ($\mathrm{ξ_{ion}}$) with the UV slope, $\mathrm{M_{UV}}$, M$_*$ or sSFR. We do find that $\mathrm{ξ_{ion}}$ correlates with [OIII]5007Å\, equivalent width (EW) (Spearman coefficient $ρ$ =0.24; p$< 4\times10^{-4}$) and H$α$ EW ($ρ$ =0.63; p$<< 1\times10^{-6}$) hold even at low EW albeit with more scatter. We also find that our novel approach to determining the ionising photon escape fraction $\mathrm{f_{esc}}$ results in values within theoretical ranges (0-10\%) though vary substantially in comparison to the empirical results (median $\mathrm{f_{esc}} = 0.9\%^{+1.1}_{-0.5}$ including non-detections, median $\mathrm{f_{esc}} = 1.9\%^{+8.9}_{-1.8}$ above a $0.01\%$ threshold). We find that this escape fraction method has consistently significant correlations with the redshift, SFR and M$_{UV}$ and sample-dependent correlations with [OIII]5007Å\,EW,H$α$ EW and stellar mass.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes 230 intermediate-redshift (1.3<z<2.6) galaxies from the OutThere survey to measure ionising photon production efficiency (ξion) and Lyman Continuum escape fraction (fesc). No significant correlations were found between ξion and UV slope, M_UV, M* or sSFR, but ξion correlates with [OIII]5007Å EW and Hα EW. The novel fesc method yields values within theoretical ranges (0-10%) with a median fesc of 0.9% (including non-detections). fesc shows consistent correlations with redshift, SFR, M_UV, and sample-dependent correlations with emission line EWs and stellar mass.
AI.motivation: To constrain the major contributors to the ionisation of the early universe, a key open question in high-redshift galaxy research, by measuring ionising photon production efficiency and Lyman Continuum escape fraction in a large, robust control sample of intermediate-redshift galaxies.
AI.method: Analysis of 230 sources (1.3<z<2.6) from the OutThere survey, a pure-parallel, wide-area JWST/NIRISS survey with JWST/NIRCam, NIRISS and HST photometry. The sample uses low threshold emission selection criteria to create a robust control sample. Ionising photon production efficiency (ξion) and Lyman Continuum escape fraction (fesc) are measured, with fesc determined via a novel approach. Correlations with spectral and physical properties are tested using Spearman correlation analysis.
AI.result: No significant correlations between ξion and UV slope, M_UV, M* or sSFR. ξion correlates with [OIII]5007Å EW (ρ=0.24, p<4×10⁻⁴) and Hα EW (ρ=0.63, p<<1×10⁻⁶), holding even at low EW with more scatter. Novel fesc method returns values within theoretical ranges (0-10%) but varying substantially from empirical results. Median fesc = 0.9%⁺¹.¹₋₀.₅ (including non-detections) and 1.9%⁺⁸.⁹₋₁.₈ (above 0.01% threshold). fesc correlates consistently with redshift, SFR, and M_UV, with sample-dependent correlations with [OIII]5007Å EW, Hα EW and stellar mass.
AI.conclusion: The study provides a large and robust control sample that verifies correlations between ionising and spectral/physical properties suggested by previous studies. ξion correlates with emission line EWs (particularly Hα), while fesc shows consistent correlations with redshift, SFR and M_UV. This provides important context for constraining the sources of ionisation in the early universe.

title: Re-evaluating the resolved mass-metallicity relation with a self-consistent metallicity calibration
comment: 13 pages, 9 figures, accepted by A&A. Comments are welcome
summary: Aims. The mass-metallicity relation (MZR) is essential for understanding the chemical evolution of galaxies. Whether the star formation rate (SFR) plays a role in setting the metallicity has long been debated. Using various metallicity calibrations can result in different conclusions for this fundamental yet unresolved issue. Methods. We apply a self-consistent metallicity calibration based on photoionization models to re-evaluate the resolved and integrated MZR. We utilize the integral field unit data from SDSS-IV/MaNGA, with $\sim 3.5\times10^6$ spaxels and $\sim$ 4550 galaxies. We compare our preferred metallicity calibration with several strong-line calibrations in the literature and direct method metallicity. We analyze the metallicity residual of MZR to evaluate the effects of SFR and apply the partial correlation coefficient to quantify the effects. Results. The metallicity calibration we used shows the best consistency with the direct method. We provide 3 equations for resolved MZR, and verify that local SFR does not show significant correlation with metallicity. Considering the integrated properties, (s)SFR do not present correlation with the metallicity residuals. The results suggest that an equilibrium of inflow and outflow is favored, and the mass-metallicity relation does not have a secondary dependence on SFR.

AI.tldr: This paper re-evaluates the mass-metallicity relation (MZR) using a self-consistent metallicity calibration based on photoionization models, applied to ~3.5 million spaxels and ~4550 galaxies from SDSS-IV/MaNGA. The authors find that neither local nor integrated star formation rate shows a significant correlation with metallicity residuals, concluding that the MZR has no secondary dependence on SFR and that an equilibrium of inflow and outflow is favored.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to resolve the long-standing debate about whether the star formation rate plays a role in setting galaxy metallicity. Since different metallicity calibrations can lead to different conclusions, they apply a self-consistent photoionization-based calibration to re-examine the resolved and integrated mass-metallicity relation.
AI.method: The authors use integral field unit data from SDSS-IV/MaNGA (~3.5 million spaxels, ~4550 galaxies). They apply a self-consistent metallicity calibration based on photoionization models, compare it with several strong-line calibrations and the direct method, analyze metallicity residuals of the MZR to evaluate SFR effects, and use partial correlation coefficients for quantification.
AI.result: The photoionization-based metallicity calibration shows the best consistency with the direct method. The authors provide 3 equations for the resolved MZR and verify that neither local SFR nor integrated (s)SFR shows significant correlation with metallicity residuals.
AI.conclusion: The mass-metallicity relation does not have a secondary dependence on the star formation rate. The findings favor an equilibrium model of gas inflow and outflow in galaxy chemical evolution.

title: The Nearby Star Formation and Supernova Histories Reconstructed from Young Star Clusters
comment: 27 pages, 9 figures. Submitted to ApJ. Comments are welcome. An interactive 3D version of Figures 2 and 3 is available at https://cswigg.github.io/cam_website/oviz_figures/oviz_supernovae.html
summary: We reconstruct the recent star formation and core-collapse supernova (ccSN) histories of the Solar Neighborhood from the past trajectories of young star clusters. Using a \textit{Gaia}-based cluster sample with newly derived ages, masses, and bulk 3D velocities, we integrate orbits backward in an assumed axisymmetric Galactic potential and combine the trajectories with IMF sampling and stellar lifetimes to infer ccSN times and locations over the past 50 Myr. The result is an all-sky, 3D, time-resolved map of nearby ccSN activity for comparison with high-resolution 3D views of the local interstellar medium. The 0--15 Myr map shows strong enhancements toward Orion, Vela, Sco--Cen, and Cepheus, many within present-day cavities and shells. At earlier times, the dominant enhancements trace the Collinder 135, Messier 6, and Alpha Persei cluster families, showing how the remnants of massive star-forming complexes have shaped the recent local feedback history. We recover a bursty star formation history followed by a delayed, smoother ccSN history. Over the last 40 Myr, the mean star formation and ccSN rates are \(823~M_\odot~\mathrm{Myr}^{-1}\) and \(7.7~\mathrm{Myr}^{-1}\), respectively, corresponding to a Milky Way rate of \(0.55\pm0.03~\mathrm{century}^{-1}\). Present-day OB-star catalogs yield rates ranging from agreement with the cluster reconstruction to several times higher. Because the catalogs overlap weakly and require different corrections, we do not rescale the ccSN map. Our reconstruction provides an empirical framework for connecting the recent history of massive-star feedback to the 3D structure and life cycle of gas in the nearby Milky Way.

AI.tldr: The paper reconstructs the recent (past 50 Myr) star formation and core-collapse supernova histories of the Solar Neighborhood by integrating backward in time the orbits of young Gaia-based star clusters with newly derived ages, masses, and 3D velocities. This yields an all-sky, 3D, time-resolved map of nearby ccSN activity, showing enhancements toward Orion, Vela, Sco-Cen, and Cepheus, and recovering a bursty star formation history followed by a smoother ccSN history with a Galactic rate of 0.55±0.03 century⁻¹.
AI.motivation: To connect the recent history of massive-star feedback to the 3D structure and life cycle of gas in the nearby Milky Way by providing an empirical map of where and when core-collapse supernovae occurred over the past 50 Myr, enabling comparison with high-resolution 3D views of the local interstellar medium.
AI.method: Using a Gaia-based young star cluster sample with newly derived ages, masses, and bulk 3D velocities, the authors integrate cluster orbits backward in an assumed axisymmetric Galactic potential. They combine these trajectories with IMF sampling and stellar lifetimes to infer ccSN times and locations over the past 50 Myr, producing a 3D time-resolved map of nearby ccSN activity.
AI.result: The 0–15 Myr map shows strong ccSN enhancements toward Orion, Vela, Sco–Cen, and Cepheus, many within present-day cavities and shells. Earlier epochs are dominated by the Collinder 135, Messier 6, and Alpha Persei cluster families. Over the last 40 Myr, the mean star formation and ccSN rates are 823 M⊙ Myr⁻¹ and 7.7 Myr⁻¹, corresponding to a Milky Way rate of 0.55±0.03 century⁻¹. Present-day OB-star catalogs yield rates ranging from agreement to several times higher.
AI.conclusion: The reconstruction provides an empirical framework for linking recent massive-star feedback to the 3D structure and life cycle of gas in the nearby Milky Way, revealing a bursty star formation history followed by a delayed, smoother ccSN history. The study does not rescale the ccSN map because present-day OB-star catalogs overlap weakly and require different corrections.

title: An Optical Illusion: High Electron Densities Create Extremely Metal-Poor Galaxy Impostors
summary: JWST has enabled the discovery of dozens of extremely metal-poor galaxies (EMPGs) with metallicities below $5\%\,Z_{\odot}$, representing a significant leap toward detecting the first galaxies without metals. However, accurate metallicity measurements require careful determination of physical conditions in the ionized gas. In this paper, we study four galaxies that appear to be EMPGs when analyzed using the direct $T_e$ method with the common low-density assumption ($n_e=10^3\,{\rm cm}^{-3}$). To test whether their metal-poor status holds when accurately measuring the density, we apply the direct method with a self-consistent determination of electron temperature ($T_e$) and density ($n_e$) in the high-ionization zone using the [OIII]$λ$5008, [OIII]$λ$4364, and [OIII]$λ$1666 lines, using JWST/NIRSpec data from the SPURS program in the Abell 2744 lensed field. We find that three out of four galaxies in our sample have extremely high electron densities ($n_e \sim 10^{5}-10^{6}\,{\rm cm^{-3}}$), which suppress the [OIII]$λ$5008 line and lead to underestimates of metallicity by up to $\sim1.1\,$dex when this density is not accounted for, and have true metallicities of 12+log(O/H) $\sim7.3-8.2$. Failure to account for high densities can therefore lead to systematic misclassification of metal-poor galaxies and biased conclusions about early chemical enrichment.

AI.tldr: JWST observations of four seemingly extremely metal-poor galaxies (EMPGs) reveal that three actually have extremely high electron densities (~10^5-10^6 cm^-3), which suppress the [OIII]λ5008 line and cause metallicity underestimates by up to ~1.1 dex. Their true metallicities are 12+log(O/H) ~7.3-8.2, not below 5% Z⊙.
AI.motivation: To test whether the EMPG classification of galaxies based on the direct T_e method with a fixed low-density assumption (n_e=10^3 cm^-3) holds when electron density is self-consistently determined, as misclassification risks biased conclusions about early chemical enrichment.
AI.method: Using JWST/NIRSpec data from the SPURS program in the Abell 2744 lensed field, the authors apply the direct T_e method with self-consistent electron temperature and density determination in the high-ionization zone using [OIII]λ5008, [OIII]λ4364, and [OIII]λ1666 lines, rather than assuming a fixed low density.
AI.result: Three of four galaxies exhibit extremely high electron densities (n_e ~10^5-10^6 cm^-3), which suppress [OIII]λ5008 and lead to metallicity underestimates up to ~1.1 dex when density is not accounted for. The true metallicities are 12+log(O/H) ~7.3-8.2, indicating these galaxies are not as metal-poor as initially classified.
AI.conclusion: Failing to account for high electron densities can systematically misclassify galaxies as metal-poor, leading to biased conclusions about early chemical enrichment. Accurate density determination is essential for reliable metallicity measurements.

title: Early Planet Formation in Embedded Disks (eDisk). XXIV: Systematic Investigation of Disk Structures based on Visibility Analysis
comment: Accept to AJ. 47 pages, 10 Figures, 8 Tables
summary: The dust continuum emission from young protostellar disks encodes key information about their mass distribution and early evolution, yet uniform high-resolution comparative studies remain limited. We present a systematic uv-plane analysis of parametric intensity models applied to ALMA Band-6 (1.3 mm) observations of 23 disks (19 protostellar systems with 4 being in binary) from the eDisk sample, spanning Gaussian profiles to power-law cores with exponential tails (PLCT), including asymmetric extensions. Gaussian models generally fail to reproduce the centrally peaked emission and extended outer structure observed in most disks, whereas the PLCT framework provides a significantly improved description of radial brightness profiles. Incorporating azimuthal asymmetries further reduces residuals in 15 of 17 inclined disks, indicating that departures from axisymmetry are common at early stages. Only two disks, L1489 IRS and Oph IRS63, exhibit clear gap and ring substructures, while most appear smooth at the spatial resolution and sensitivity of our observations. These systems are among the most evolved in the sample, and the absence of flat-spectrum sources limits the evolutionary range probed, {suggesting that the detection of prominent gaps and rings is not common} in the earliest phases of disk evolution. Using a uniform definition of disk radius based on the 95\% enclosed flux, we find a positive correlation with stellar mass, $R_{\rm disk} \propto M_{\star}^{1.5 \pm 0.1}$, with disks in binary systems systematically smaller than those around isolated protostars. While the models capture overall morphology and large-scale asymmetries, distinguishing intrinsic structures from radiative transfer effects in optically thick regions remains challenging.

AI.tldr: This study presents a systematic uv-plane analysis of parametric intensity models applied to ALMA Band-6 observations of 23 protostellar disks from the eDisk sample. The PLCT framework outperforms Gaussian models in describing disk morphology, azimuthal asymmetries are common (15/17 inclined disks), only two disks show gap/ring substructures, disk radii follow R ∝ M*^1.5, and binary disks are systematically smaller than isolated ones.
AI.motivation: Young protostellar disk dust continuum emission encodes crucial information about mass distribution and early evolution, yet uniform high-resolution comparative studies across a large sample remain limited. The authors seek to fill this gap with a systematic analysis of early-stage disks.
AI.method: The authors apply parametric intensity models in the uv-plane to ALMA Band-6 (1.3 mm) observations of 23 disks (19 protostellar systems, 4 in binaries) from the eDisk sample. Models range from Gaussian profiles to power-law cores with exponential tails (PLCT), including asymmetric extensions. Disk radii are uniformly defined using 95% enclosed flux.
AI.result: Gaussian models fail to reproduce observed morphologies; PLCT significantly improves fits. Azimuthal asymmetries reduce residuals in 15 of 17 inclined disks. Only L1489 IRS and Oph IRS63 show gaps/rings. A positive correlation R_disk ∝ M*^(1.5±0.1) is found, and binary disks are systematically smaller.
AI.conclusion: Prominent gaps and rings are not common in the earliest phases of disk evolution; most protostellar disks appear smooth at the resolution/sensitivity probed. Distinguishing intrinsic structures from radiative transfer effects in optically thick regions remains a challenge, and flat-spectrum sources are absent from the sample, limiting the evolutionary range examined.
